blocks.text: The questions that begin here belong to a larger series of divine speeches that range across the earth’s foundations, the sea, weather, stars, and wild creatures. They answer Job personally, but they do not disclose the heavenly challenge or provide a simple cause for his suffering. Readers have understood this creation tour in several, not necessarily competing, ways: it may expose the limits of Job’s knowledge, portray the value and freedom of nonhuman life, challenge Job’s proposed governance, or offer encounter rather than explanation.

When Job’s steadfastness is discussed across the whole book, it need not mean silent acceptance of abuse or a refusal to seek safety and protection. It can refer instead to persistence through suffering and to the story’s eventual outcome. A later passage groups Job with the prophets in connection with suffering, patience, endurance, and the Lord’s compassionate outcome.

sections.title: The Divine Speeches in Job’s Story
